source: Siskind (2001) Grounding the Lexical Semantics of Verbs in Visual Perception using Force Dynamics and Event Logic (LEONARD)
finding: Older AI system that recognises verbs from video by tracking changes in force-dynamic relations (support, contact, attachment), not motion profile. Event logic combines primitive events into compound ones.
numbers: 7 event types (pick up, put down, stack, unstack, move, assemble, disassemble); 35 movies, 5 per type, one subject. 6 false negatives, 0 false positives. 4 of the 6 misses were for assemble, 1 for move, 1 for unstack.
quote: Using force dynamics and event logic ... allows the system to be more robust than prior systems based on motion profile.
limits: Siskind uses force dynamics in a narrower sense (support, contact, attachment) than Talmy (allowing, preventing, forcing). Preliminary test, one subject, lab blocks. Author says a larger evaluation is future work.
agent_relevance: Force-dynamic state changes give a verb check that is robust to surface variation with no false positives. An agent could verify a claimed action by checking required state changes, not appearance.

source: Siskind (2001) LEONARD design claims versus HMM motion-profile approach
finding: Author argues force-dynamic features beat motion profile in three ways: tolerate wider motion variance, reject non-events whose motion looks like half of two events, and detect all simultaneous or nested events.
numbers: Non-event demo (Figure 2): two sequences each match the first half of one event and the second half of another under motion profile; force-dynamic logic rejects both. Feature count is quadratic in participants for both approaches.
limits: Argument and demos, not a head-to-head benchmark with numbers.
agent_relevance: Design pattern: require the full chain of state changes (cause then effect) before accepting an event. Maps to a verification step that rejects look-alike partial chains.

source: Dunietz, Levin, Carbonell (2017) The BECauSE Corpus 2.0: Annotating Causality and Overlapping Relations
finding: Causal-language corpus with three types (CONSEQUENCE, MOTIVATION, PURPOSE) and two degrees: FACILITATE vs INHIBIT, a force-dynamics-like split between positive and inhibitory causation.
numbers: 5380 sentences, 1803 causal instances; 1634 (90.7%) have both cause and effect; 587 involve overlapping relations. Agreement: causal connective F1 0.77 (0.70 in v1.0); relation-type kappa about 0.7 (0.8 in v1.0); degrees close to full agreement; overlapping connective F1 0.89. IAA sample 260 sentences, 98 causal instances.
quote: The scheme also distinguishes positive causation (FACILITATE) from inhibitory causation (INHIBIT)
limits: News and legal-style text, agent heavy. Two annotators. Facilitate/inhibit is a two-way split; Talmy's letting, hindering and despite are not annotated.
agent_relevance: A usable scheme to tag claims in a reasoning trace as facilitate or inhibit. Humans label the degree reliably.

source: Dunietz et al. (2017) BECauSE 2.0 corpus statistics on motivation and temporal piggybacking
finding: Real text frames causes as agent motivation a lot, and causal meaning often rides on temporal or hypothetical words.
numbers: Nearly 45% of causal instances are MOTIVATION or PURPOSE; over 14% of causal expressions are piggybacked on temporal relations; 463 of 718 hypothetical-relation annotations are non-causal.
limits: Politics and economics text may bias toward agents. Counts cover only constructions that can express causality.
agent_relevance: Causal cues in text are mixed with time and condition. A parser reading force-dynamic claims must separate them.

source: Butnaru, Creanga, Dinu (2026) Larry Caused the Car to Stop, But the Model Didn't Notice: Transformer Blindness to the M-Heuristic
finding: Encoder NLI models ignore the difference between lexical causatives (Larry stopped the car) and periphrastic ones (Larry caused the car to stop), which humans link to direct vs mediated causation.
numbers: 188 items, 15 verbs, 2x2 design. DeBERTa-v3-large 0/188 (all Neutral); RoBERTa-large 5/188 (2.7%); BART-large 0/188. Chance is 33% (3-way) or 50%.
limits: NLI framing with pragmatic gold labels; small verb set; Wolff's human data cited second-hand. Preprint, CLiC-it 2026.
agent_relevance: Direct vs indirect causation encoded in wording is not used by default. A scaffold must ask for it.

source: Butnaru et al. (2026) Gemini Flash-Lite prompt regimes on causative items
finding: Same LLM goes from 0 to 100 percent depending on prompt: knowledge of the causative contrast is present but unused under plain NLI.
numbers: Gemini Flash-Lite on 188 items: direct NLI 0/188 (0.0%, all NEUTRAL); chain-of-thought 41/188 (21.8%); metalinguistic prompt stating the M-Heuristic with Larry/car examples 188/188 (100.0%) with item-specific reasoning traces.
quote: Metalinguistic prompts reach 100% with item-specific traces.
limits: One model. The metalinguistic prompt gives the rule and examples, so 100% shows rule application, not discovery. Generic CoT recovered little.
agent_relevance: Strong scaffold evidence: naming the distinction and giving a worked contrast beats generic step-by-step reasoning (100 vs 21.8).

source: Butnaru et al. (2026) probing and embedding control experiments
finding: A linear probe on DeBERTa seemed to find the causative distinction, but a syntactic-complexity control showed it tracked syntax, not causation type. Embeddings group periphrastic causatives with manner descriptions in the direction opposite to the prediction.
numbers: Probes at all 24 layers; original probe reached 100% at some layers; at layer 4 control probe 87.5% vs causative 100%. Similarity over 30 triplets: wrong grouping in 29/30 (96.7%).
limits: Small triplet set. Embedding similarity is a weak proxy.
agent_relevance: Do not trust a probe or a high accuracy without a control that varies surface form but not meaning.

source: Wolff's causative-language experiment as reported by Butnaru et al. (2026)
finding: Human baseline: people choose lexical causatives for unmediated causal chains and periphrastic causatives for mediated chains (no-intervening-cause idea).
numbers: Unmediated events: lexical 58%, periphrastic 38%. Mediated events: periphrastic 85%, lexical 5%.
limits: Second-hand figures from the machine paper's description of Wolff, not the original paper; check against the human-data files for this subfield.
agent_relevance: Gives a human benchmark for testing an agent's direct-versus-mediated causal language.

source: Weissweiler, Koksal, Schutze (2024) Hybrid Human-LLM Corpus Construction and LLM Evaluation for Rare Linguistic Phenomena (caused-motion)
finding: LLMs struggle to see that a caused-motion construction (she sneezed the foam off the cappuccino) adds a motion meaning: a force-transmission pattern carried by the construction, not the verb.
numbers: 765 hand-annotated sentences. Share answering yes both before and after swapping in a prototypical motion verb (understands the construction): Mixtral-8x7b-IT 69.75%, Mistral-7b-IT 68.12%, GPT-4 57.07%, GPT-3.5 43.20%, Gemini Pro 43.43%; Llama2-7b base 9.54%, Llama2-13b chat 5.59%.
limits: Tests the construction, not Talmy force dynamics by name. Prompting only; GPT-4 trails Mistral. Error over 30% even for the best.
agent_relevance: Models miss force and motion that grammar supplies. A scaffold should ask what the push did, not what the verb usually means.

source: Nie, Zhang, Amdekar, Piech, Hashimoto, Gerstenberg (2023) MoCa: Human-LLM alignment on causal and moral judgment
finding: LLMs agree with human causal-selection judgments only modestly and weigh factors differently from people. Personal force is one factor in the moral tasks; only ChatGPT and GPT-4 matched humans on it.
numbers: Stories from 24 cognitive-science papers. Discrete agreement on causal judgment: GPT-4 43.1 +/-5.9, GPT-3.5-davinci-v3 41.3, Claude-v1 36.1, GPT-3.5-turbo 35.4, GPT-2/RoBERTa about 34-35. Persona prompts moved moral agreement by up to 18.6 points but barely moved causal judgment. Prompt search found 'James is a consequentialist', +8.1 points on moral agreement.
limits: Text vignettes; PDF table layout partly garbled, so exact column mapping for some models is uncertain.
agent_relevance: Prompt framing moves moral but not causal alignment. The paper names force transfer as a normative frame for causal selection (Wolff 2007).

source: Kiciman, Ness, Sharma, Tan (2023) Causal Reasoning and Large Language Models: Opening a New Frontier for Causality
finding: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 do well on text causal tasks, including necessary and sufficient cause in vignettes with preemption and prevention (logic that Talmy force dynamics covers informally).
numbers: Pairwise causal discovery 97% (13 points above prior); counterfactual reasoning 92% (20 points above); necessary/sufficient cause on 15 standard vignettes: gpt-4 86.6%, gpt-3.5-turbo 46.6% (below chance).
limits: 15 vignettes only; authors note unpredictable failure modes (for example short-circuit vignettes). Contamination possible on standard vignettes.
agent_relevance: Reasoning about prevention and preemption is reachable with a strong model but not a weak one. Use counterfactual necessity and sufficiency questions as explicit checks.

source: Jin et al. (2023) CLadder: Assessing Causal Reasoning in Language Models
finding: 10K formal causal questions in words; GPT-4 is only modestly above chance; a structured causal chain-of-thought lifts it.
numbers: CausalCoT 70.40% overall, +8.37 points over vanilla GPT-4. LLaMa, Alpaca and non-instruction GPT-3 near random (about 44-53). CausalCoT by rung: 83.35 / 67.47 / 62.05, falling as rungs rise.
limits: Formal Pearl-style questions, not force-dynamic prevention verbs. Table text layout garbled; headline numbers taken from prose and the CausalCoT row.
agent_relevance: A scaffold that forces graph, query type, formal estimand then computation gives about 8 points. Matches our idea of making the structure explicit.

source: Carro et al. (2025) Do LLMs Show Biases in Causal Learning? Insights from Contingency Judgment
finding: On 1000 null-contingency medical scenarios, all three LLMs infer a causal effect that is not there (illusion of causality).
numbers: GPT-4o-mini median 75.7 (95% CI 75.0-76.5), 0% zero ratings; Claude-3.5-Sonnet median 50.0, 4.6% zeros; Gemini-1.5-Pro median 45.0, 20.5% zeros (scale 0-100, normative answer 0).
limits: Contingency learning, not force dynamics. Chain-of-thought not tested; authors list it as future work.
agent_relevance: Models assign a push to a cause with no evidence. A scaffold should demand a with/without comparison before claiming a causal force.

source: Kementchedjhieva, Anderson, Sogaard (2021) John praised Mary because he? Implicit causality bias in LMs
finding: Verbs carry a built-in direction of cause (subject vs object). Language models encode it, and bidirectional ones over-rely on it when a clause states the opposite cause.
numbers: 6 PLMs (BERT, RoBERTa-L, GPT, GPT2-M, ELECTRA, ELECTRA-L); all correlate significantly with human IC bias on 305 data points (Spearman, p<0.001); bidirectional moderate to strong, unidirectional weak. Coreference accuracy above the 50% baseline in all, lower in incongruent contexts, largest gap for ELECTRA.
limits: Small dataset (305). Old models (2018-2020). The link to human reading delay is partly hypothesis.
agent_relevance: Lexical cues in verbs can override explicit causal text. A scaffold should check a stated cause against the verb's default direction.

source: Bear et al. (2021) Physion: Evaluating Physical Prediction from Vision in Humans and Machines
finding: Humans predict collisions, rolling, support and similar physical outcomes well; vision models without object-level state do poorly.
numbers: Human accuracy 0.71 across eight scenarios (t=27.5, p<1e-7); object-centric models beat others but stay below humans; graph networks with direct physical state are best and most human-like; models with only convolutional latents near chance.
limits: Rendered simulations; not a language task.
agent_relevance: The bottleneck is extracting object and force state, which text-only agents never see.

source: Yi et al. (2020) CLEVRER: CoLlision Events for Video REpresentation and Reasoning
finding: Video QA on colliding objects: models do well on description but badly on explaining what caused what, predicting and counterfactuals.
numbers: Best baseline MAC(V+): descriptive 86.4; explanatory 70.5 per option, 22.3 per question; predictive 59.7 / 42.9; counterfactual 63.5 / 25.1. Neuro-symbolic NS-DR: descriptive 88.1; explanatory 87.6 / 79.6; predictive 82.9 / 68.7; counterfactual 74.1 / 42.2.
limits: Synthetic scenes, 2019 models. Per-question score needs all options right. Column mapping read from garbled table.
agent_relevance: Explicit dynamics plus symbolic causal logic gives big gains on causal questions (22.3 to 79.6 per-question, explanatory). Supports an explicit dynamics step.

source: Liu et al. (2022) Mind's Eye: Grounded Language Model Reasoning through Simulation
finding: Giving a language model the output of a physics engine (MuJoCo) makes it much better at physical reasoning questions; a force-and-motion tool loop around an LLM.
numbers: UTOPIA benchmark, 39 sub-tasks, 6 scenes. GPT-3 175B vanilla 24% zero-shot, 38.2% few-shot. Mind's Eye: +27.9 points zero-shot, +46.0 few-shot on average. GPT-3 1.3B + Mind's Eye 29.8% vs vanilla GPT-3 175B 29% zero-shot (about 100x smaller).
limits: Questions auto-generated from the engine, so engine and questions share assumptions. 2022 models. Needs an engine per domain.
agent_relevance: Strongest example of tool-grounded physics inside a reasoning loop. A simulator call beat model scale.

source: Ballout, Jassim, Bruni (2025) Pixels to Principles: Probing Intuitive Physics in Multimodal Language Models
finding: Video MLLMs fail to tell physically plausible from implausible clips; vision encoders hold the cue but the language model does not use it.
numbers: GRASP and IntPhys 2. Human accuracy about 80%. InternVL 2.5, Qwen 2.5 VL, LLaVA-OneVision, Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking do not exceed 54%. IntPhys 2 largest models up to 52%; Qwen 2.5 VL 3B 51.5% with CoT. Best scene cases: 68.9% Gravity-Inertia (Qwen 7B), 97.7% Gravity-Support (InternVL 78B with CoT).
limits: Binary plausibility judgement, simulated scenes. CoT help small on average.
agent_relevance: Information present in perception can be unused downstream. Add an explicit step that reads off force relations.

source: Schulze Buschoff, Voudouris, Demircan, Schulz (2026) Can Vision Language Models Learn Intuitive Physics from Interaction?
finding: Reinforcement learning from interaction raises within-task accuracy but does not give physical intuitions that transfer to related tasks.
numbers: No single headline figure extracted; abstract states models trained on one task do not reliably generalise to related tasks sharing visual statistics and physics, with or without interaction.
limits: Read abstract, introduction and conclusions only; numbers not extracted. Training-time method, not a prompt scaffold.
agent_relevance: Training for one physical task will not give general force reasoning, so a scaffold or tool is the safer lever.

source: Li et al. (2026) Beyond Static Vision: Scene Dynamic Field Unlocks Intuitive Physics in MLLMs (ICLR 2026)
finding: State-of-the-art MLLMs do poorly on fluid and continuum dynamics (next-frame selection, temporal coherence). Fine-tuning with physics-simulator data helps.
numbers: Scene Dynamic Field gives up to 20.7% gains on fluid tasks with generalisation to unseen physical domains; baseline numbers not extracted.
limits: Fine-tuning not prompting; fluids rather than discrete push or block events.
agent_relevance: Simulator-derived data lifts physical judgement, again pointing at a tool or simulator step.

source: Gillman et al. (2025) Force Prompting: Video Generation Models Can Learn and Generalize Physics-based Control Signals
finding: Force vectors (point pokes, global wind) used as control input to video generators; models generalise from few synthetic objects and show some mass sensitivity (same force moves a lighter object further).
numbers: About 15k training examples (23k for the local-force set), one day on four A100 GPUs. Reported to beat trajectory-based baselines on force adherence and realism in human evaluation.
limits: Generation, not language reasoning; force here is physical, not Talmy's psychological force. Evaluation numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Machine use of explicit force vectors as an interface. The vector view of force (as in Wolff's model) can be implemented.

source: Sang (2025) Constructing the Umwelt: Cognitive Planning through Belief-Intent Co-Evolution
finding: Driving-planner paper that cites Talmy's Force Dynamics as the basis of a 'Force Composition' causal model beside symbolic deduction and probabilistic induction, but loosely: gradient flow is called a 'Causal Corrective Force'.
numbers: Evaluated on nuPlan; the abstract and text read give no ablation of the force-dynamics part and no numbers for it.
limits: Metaphorical use; no test of the force-dynamics claim. Treat as a citation, not evidence.
agent_relevance: Shows how the theory gets borrowed loosely. Do not count it as a validated method.

source: Wu and Lu (2026) CauProphet: Teaching Agents to Develop Causal Cognition like Humans
finding: LLM agent builds a persistent Causal Belief (factors and effects of possible actions) and updates it across tasks.
numbers: Finance: 25.4% improvement in mean rank correlation with next-day returns over a baseline agent; prediction accuracy 21.3% to 28.6% in a dynamic real-world setting.
limits: Abstract page only. Not force dynamics by name; no enable/prevent typing.
agent_relevance: An agent loop that keeps typed causal beliefs beats raw memory. A force-type label (cause, enable, prevent) could be a field in that belief.

source: Luo et al. (2026) The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
finding: Video world models do not flip predictions when a tiny change flips the true future (box millimetres past a table edge).
numbers: 11 models, 1,680 initial frames over 10 simulated and 15 real tasks. Best pair accuracy 18.3%, below 25% random. A VLM was selective near the boundary; a coding agent that measures the image came close to the true boundary.
limits: Abstract page only. Video models, not text LLMs.
agent_relevance: Where a decision depends on a threshold such as support or balance, measuring beats predicting. Tool use beats free prediction.

source: Search log (2026-11-17) for LLM studies using Talmy force dynamics by name
url: arxiv.org title and abstract searches; crossref
finding: No paper found that tests language models on Talmy's force-dynamic categories (letting, hindering, despite) or uses force-dynamic labels inside an LLM agent loop. Closest hits: Butnaru 2026 (causatives), Weissweiler 2024 (caused-motion), MoCa 2023 (force in causal selection), Siskind 2001 (video).
numbers: arXiv searches for 'force dynamics' returned mostly physics; combined Talmy searches returned none. Crossref returned linguistics chapters only.
limits: Search was thin: the WebSearch budget was exhausted and Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex were rate-limited. The gap may be partly a search artefact.
agent_relevance: Treat force dynamics as a design idea to test, not a method with LLM evidence. First experiment: a cause/enable/prevent probe set with and without a metalinguistic prompt.

source: Crossref listing: Event structure, force dynamics and verb semantics (Language Sciences 2024); Event Causation and Force Dynamics in Argument Structure Constructions (2020)
finding: Linguistics work continues to link force dynamics with verb and construction semantics; titles found, full texts not opened.
limits: Metadata only. Pointers for the other angles.
agent_relevance: Possible sources for a lexicon of force-dynamic verbs to seed prompts.
